replacements.text: The grilling board sent a typed answer to its slower expert seat only when the answer marked or opened a decision. Any answer carrying a note or free text now goes to the expert. The rules that escalated a typed answer on the board's map can no longer fire. Their code remains.
Six new unit tests cover the change. Before the change, four of them failed.

The expert picks the effort by one rule. A turn that carries an impact task runs at the task effort on every channel, including one the human moved to the expert. A typed turn with no task runs at the task effort on a channel the human has not moved. The human chose the heavy effort for a channel they moved to the expert themselves. The same turn therefore runs at the heavy effort on that channel. A channel the escalation policy moved counts as not moved by the human.

The expert driver tells a human move from a policy move off the log, at the moment it picks the effort. It uses the two readings the escalation module already provides. When nothing is downstream of a typed answer, no impact task is recorded. Under that same condition, nothing waits.

Every map answer carrying text goes straight to the expert. The map's first seat therefore never reads the human's prose from this change on. The map's prose escalation conditions are therefore unreachable there. Threads keep them. Pruning their code and the page's map-toggle highlight is separate work. Their code and the page's map-toggle highlight therefore stay.

The three amended passages sit in two specs. Each now cites PND-D4 (the spec decision that seats every typed answer on the expert). They are GUI-A33 (the criterion on highlighting a channel's way to the expert), GUI-D48 (the decision on which channels the escalation conditions reach) and that decision's third trigger.

Six existing tests used a typed map answer only as a vehicle. Those tests now pick a plain option. Five tests of the map's prose conditions now run on a thread. One browser test moved to a thread. That browser test was renamed. Its evidence row was re-pointed. In the evidence ledgers, PND-A2 (the criterion on seating a typed answer) goes from open to twelve test rows. PND-A11 (the criterion on the backpressure paragraph) goes from open to four test rows.
A typed answer with nothing downstream goes to the expert. Such an answer records no task. Such an answer makes nothing wait.

Any answer carrying a note or free text goes to the expert. With nothing downstream, the turn produces neither a recorded impact task nor a wait. A typed turn with no task uses the task effort or, on a channel the human moved to the expert, the heavy effort. Three spec passages now say the same.

make ci exits 0. make e2e-grillui exits 0 with 97 passed. Six new unit tests cover the change. Before the change, four of them failed. The map's escalation rules are now unreachable. Their code is not removed. No review round ran.

questions.question: Please add a separate Heads-up row for the caveat that the map's unreachable escalation rules remain in the code.
